tk-78qg2my.title: Rule on 4 track epics left in a paused project, so the Delivery layer's first Delivery can close (dissolve all four recommended)
tk-78qg2my.line2:
The Delivery layer's first Delivery (tk-wmwcdlc.3) closes only once no open child epic lacks both an Aim line and a hypothesis. Four still do: Tracks 2 to 5 under the live-site eval remediation epic ([another rig's bead]). Their rig is suspended, and the epic is parked. Once the board-wording Story (unit 4) lands, this is the Delivery's last open Story, so the Delivery's checkpoint, one of the two hand runs the checkpoint machinery waits for, waits on this ruling.

Recommended: dissolve all four. The epic grouped its tracks by what gated the work, and each of those gates has since cleared or moved. Track 5's 14 members are all closed. The 7 open members of Tracks 2 to 4 move directly under the epic, whose park keeps holding them. Three of them are already grouped by integration efforts of their own, and the other four are decisions you hold. The brief, with each track's facts and the exact writes, is in this Story's notes and on the conversation queued on the epic.

Where to hold the sitting:
A (recommended). Engage this gate here. The sitting runs in gc-toolkit and writes into the paused rig's store, which needs none of that rig's agents. Its record sits on a gc-toolkit conversation rather than on the epic's own, which is where this departs from the design.
B. Resume the rig, engage the conversation queued on the epic, then suspend the rig again. While it runs, its standing sessions start and its refinery takes up one routed bug, a PR approved and waiting to merge.
C. Leave it until the rig resumes for its own work. The Delivery and its checkpoint wait that long.

However it is held, the sitting clears this gate once its writes read back: tk-wmwcdlc.3.5 waits on it, and clearing it re-slings tk-wmwcdlc.3.5, whose run checks that no such child epic is left and closes it. To stand down instead, do not clear this gate: run "$(gc gc-toolkit scripts-dir)/stand-down.sh" tk-wmwcdlc.3.5 --key child-epic-sitting --ruling '<why>'.

tk-8iy0jh6.title: Five epics in [another rig] and [another rig]: two standing subjects and three finished epics
tk-8iy0jh6.line2:
Five epics in [another rig] and [another rig] still lack what an epic needs: a hypothesis, or a ruling that closed it. Both rigs were paused when the hypothesis cleanup asked you about each epic on 2026-11-06, so their epics were left until they ran again. Both run now. On PR #1392 you wrote: "An Epic without a hypothesis is incomplete and should be fixed to include a hypothesis" (review comment 4450631154). Once the stricter epic check lands (tk-wmwcdlc.6), the doctor reports each of the three closed ones as an error.

Two standing subjects are typed as epics. Each says it never closes, so neither has a hypothesis to answer:
- [another rig] UI ([another rig's bead]): "Standing subject for [another rig] UI feedback and its dispositions. ... The subject itself never closes." It has no members, and its last visit was on 2026-08-09.
- The layers of material Inkling manages ([another rig's bead]): "STANDING STRATEGY SUBJECT. Not an implementation bead." Both its members are closed, and its notes say its deliverable landed on 2026-08-19 ([another rig] PR #533).

Three finished epics carry no close ruling. Agents closed them as complete, and none of their records quotes you:
- Epic 6 Polish ([another rig's bead]), closed 2026-08-09: all 16 follow-up stories closed. Its close note says you closed it at visit [another rig's bead] rather than name a next slice, and records no words of yours.
- Controller connection storm ([another rig's bead]), closed 2026-07-14: the storm that saturated the shared Dolt server was resolved by two fixes in bd, one for a connection leak and one for a costly per-connection probe. Both are in upstream bd's own source (v1.3.1: the storeReady guard in internal/storage/dolt/store.go and the SHOW COLUMNS probe in internal/storage/schema/schema.go), and the city runs a later release, 1.3.4. Its note reads "operator-ratified by Zook" and cites no sitting.
- Self-close runtime kill ([another rig's bead]), closed 2026-06-03: a session that closed itself was killed partway through its own close. That is fixed. What runs today is upstream Gas City's own fix (its PR #2665), which stops a session with the calling process left out (internal/runtime/tmux/adapter.go:338 in [another rig] at 36ad5186a), not the reorder the epic made. Its close reason records your decision of 2026-06-02 to defer the epic's upstream PR, with no sitting or quote behind it.

A. As recommended: retype both standing subjects as tasks, and record the three finished epics as closed with the outcomes above. It costs you a yes. The two subjects keep their notes and stay where conversations about them open. Only their type changes, so they stop reading as incomplete epics.
Record it. For each subject: gc bd --rig [another rig] update <subject> --type task --append-notes "<the ruling, with this conversation's id>". For each finished epic, the close as the converse-epic-review skill records one, with epic_ruling=close, epic_ruling_reason="Done: <its outcome>" and epic_ruling_evidence=tk-v94mnsx.

B. Close a standing subject as not an epic, or give a finished epic another outcome. It costs you that ruling for each one you name. A closed subject's notes stay readable, and later conversations open on beads of their own.

Two more asks from the same re-check are separate, because each needs its own rig's sitting: the security hardening epic in [another rig] ([another rig's bead]) and the live-site remediation epic in [another rig] ([another rig's bead]). [another rig] is still paused, and its five such epics wait until it runs again.

Answering: this conversation replies to gate tk-v94mnsx, which tk-wmwcdlc.5 waits on, so your sign-off with --ruled yes answers it once all five are recorded.

tk-yhquh93.title: Epic: Board UI design
tk-yhquh93.line2: If the board is designed as a whole, from prototypes you react to, instead of one change at a time, you can read it and get around in it easily; we'll know it worked when board changes stop coming back from your review for how they look and work.

contract.hypothesis: If the board is designed as a whole, from prototypes you react to, instead of one change at a time, you can read it and get around in it easily; we'll know it worked when board changes stop coming back from your review for how they look and work.
contract.boundaries: Cut on the board's web page: how it looks and behaves, and the one read that feeds it. In: the design (the operator's Claude Design session and their rulings of 2026-11-11), building it as the board's only web page, and the page's read, which is one read per rig of the bead graph whose every state is the answer of the pack's shared readers and which adds no rule, no stored state and no new concept. Beside it: what the board must tell you about where things stand is tk-ikpyzn's, and what it marks as needing you is tk-99h9ijx's; the page draws both from the shared readers and decides neither. Not its work: the board's direct store reader and its pack-stamped rows, which tk-1tfzr71.24 retires and the command-line board reads until then, and the parity test that holds the Go contract and its hand-written TypeScript mirror equal, which tk-1tfzr71.25 retires. The page reads neither and gives them no new work.
contract.indicators: Design complaints in the operator's reviews of board changes. Baseline: PR #774 ("word vomit on the page") and PR #911 ("pretty poor"). Bar: the first five board changes after the design is built draw no complaint on a point the design settled.
contract.ruling_reason: The operator's go on building their own Claude Design export as one pull request that replaces the board's web page and adds its one read (conversation tk-w2hvygn, 2026-11-11). The hypothesis stands; the course and the boundaries change. Shift is this sitting's reading: they did not use the word.
